prompt:

A vemi allocates appointments among groups.
A group receives an appointment only when all its members approve.
Adding a member cancels all previous approvals until everyone approves again.

Create one metaphor to explain this system, and explain the relationships it captures. Answer in 100–120 words.
Use a familiar real-world process whose ordinary behavior supports the comparison. Do not invent magical or physically impossible behavior to restate a rule. If a system rule has no good counterpart in that process, identify the limitation explicitly rather than making up a matching behavior.
response:
Imagine this system as a potluck dinner planning process. Each dish represents an appointment, and each group member must agree on it before it can be included. If a new person joins the planning, all previous dish agreements are canceled, and everyone must agree again on the meal menu. 

This metaphor captures the idea of consensus: just as a potluck requires everyone’s approval to finalize the menu, an appointment needs unanimous group consent. The limitation here is the automated cancellation of all approvals when a new member joins; in a real potluck, previous agreements might not be automatically discarded but rather renegotiated. This highlights the system's need for fresh consensus with any change.
